00216.label: Capecitabine · active treatment cycle

medicines.name: Metoclopramide
medicines.dose: 10 mg PO up to three times daily as required
medicines.note: One option for oral minimal-low risk; check renal function, contraindications, interactions and duration. Do not add all alternatives concurrently.

additional_support: The team agrees a rescue medicine if needed; routine daily anti-sickness prevention is not automatically required for this oral low-risk schedule.
Report diarrhoea promptly and follow the written rescue plan. Severe symptoms, fever, dehydration or inability to drink need urgent advice.
White-cell growth-factor injections are prescribed according to individual risk and previous complications. They are not automatically required for every patient or every cycle.
Use gentle skin and mouth care. Painful hands and feet or mouth sores can require a tablet hold and team review; do not continue simply to finish the pack.

Where prescribed under the capecitabine source: loperamide 4 mg initially then 2 mg after each loose stool, maximum 16 mg/day; follow the written local escalation plan. Do not copy the irinotecan high-dose schedule.
Swallow capecitabine whole with water and food or within 30 minutes afterwards. Do not crush or cut tablets; missed toxicity doses are not replaced.

Interrupt immediately for moderate/severe toxicity and obtain oncology advice. Grade 2 or worse dehydration requires interruption until rehydrated and the cause is controlled; do not restart automatically after the planned break.

Record previous dose reductions before prescribing the next cycle. A table percentage must not automatically re-escalate a toxicity-reduced dose. Partial-DPD starting-dose titration is a separate specialist pathway.
Confirm blood count, renal and liver profile before every cycle; DPD testing precedes first treatment unless already tested. Plan INR checks if a vitamin K antagonist is used.

guidance.label: NCCP Classification V6 (2025), oral minimal-to-low risk Table 5

00692.label: Day 1 · chemotherapy and antibody

medicines.name: Chlorphenamine
medicines.timing: At least one hour before cetuximab
medicines.note: Repeat for subsequent cetuximab infusions; assess prior infusion reactions.

medicines.name: Dexamethasone
medicines.timing: At least one hour before cetuximab on Day 1
medicines.note: This corticosteroid also covers the treatment-day corticosteroid part of antiemesis where appropriate. Pharmacy must reconcile route, dose and timing; do not automatically add a second 8 mg antiemetic dose.

medicines.name: Ondansetron
medicines.note: NCIS V8 moderate-risk row; consider QT risk, low electrolytes, interactions and the individual prescription.

medicines.name: Dexamethasone
medicines.timing: Days 2 and 3 after the administered Day 1 chemotherapy
medicines.note: NCIS V8 delayed prophylaxis. Reconcile with any other steroid prescription; re-anchor dates if treatment is delayed.

medicines.name: Metoclopramide
medicines.dose: 10 mg PO up to three times daily as required
medicines.timing: Rescue nausea treatment only as prescribed
medicines.note: NCIS V8 rescue option; check contraindications, renal function, interactions and prescribed duration.

additional_support: Antiemetic classification refers to the active treatment day. Reconcile duplicate steroid entries before prescribing.
No automatic G-CSF schedule is added; use the patient’s neutropenia history, risk and consultant plan.
Cetuximab premedication and infusion observation remain necessary even on an antibody-only day.
Start local EGFR skin care; monitor magnesium, calcium and potassium before and periodically during therapy, then monthly for two months after the final dose.

Cold exposure can precipitate oxaliplatin neurotoxicity; do not recommend ice chips during fluorouracil in this combination. Review neuropathy every two cycles and sooner if symptoms interfere with function.
Confirm line care, pump contact details and disconnection arrangements; report chest pain, severe early fluorouracil toxicity or pump/line problems urgently.

NCCP 00692 v2 p1 permits omitting observation after two tolerated cetuximab doses, whereas current EMA Erbitux SmPC sections 4.2/4.4 require monitoring during and for at least one hour after every infusion. Reconcile this conflict with oncology pharmacy/local policy; do not automatically waive monitoring. Chemotherapy must start no earlier than one hour after cetuximab ends.
FOLFOX4 uses two separate 22-hour fluorouracil infusions on Days 1 and 2, with a second treatment visit; never substitute a single 46-hour modified-FOLFOX6 pump schedule.
Cetuximab and FOLFOX may be delayed independently. Reconcile actual treatment days, component-specific recovery and previous dose changes before updating support prescriptions.
Intolerable cetuximab skin reactions require interruption even when graded below 3 under the EMA product information; review infection and supportive skin care promptly.

guidance.label: NCCP NCIS antiemetics V8 (2025), Table 1 and multi-day principles

00692.label: Day 2 · FOLFOX4 fluorouracil; confirm complete prescription
00692.emetogenic_risk: Low treatment-day risk; delayed Day 1 moderate-risk coverage still applies

medicines.name: Dexamethasone
medicines.timing: Day 2; already part of the Day 1 moderate-risk Days 2–3 plan
medicines.note: Reconcile this single dose across both plans; do not issue an additional duplicate dose.

medicines.name: Metoclopramide
medicines.dose: 10 mg PO up to three times daily as required
medicines.note: Review persistent nausea, hydration and individual contraindications.

additional_support: NCCP 00692 v2 p1 lists fluorouracil bolus and a separate 22-hour infusion on Day 2, but lists folinic acid on Day 1 only. Confirm the intended Day 2 folinic-acid prescription with the consultant and oncology pharmacy; do not infer or silently add a Day 2 dose from a generic FOLFOX4 schedule.
No repeat cetuximab or oxaliplatin is scheduled on Day 2.
NCIS multi-day guidance: cover the risk on each administered treatment day and delayed risk after treatment, using a reconciled prescription.

guidance.label: NCCP NCIS V8 multi-day SACT principles

00692.label: Day 8 · weekly cetuximab only

medicines.name: Chlorphenamine
medicines.timing: At least one hour before cetuximab

medicines.name: Dexamethasone
medicines.timing: At least one hour before cetuximab
medicines.note: Reconcile low-risk antiemesis with this corticosteroid; do not duplicate steroids.

medicines.name: Metoclopramide
medicines.dose: 10 mg PO up to three times daily as required
medicines.note: No automatic delayed steroid course is carried over from Day 1 chemotherapy.

additional_support: Cetuximab only: no irinotecan, oxaliplatin, fluorouracil or atropine is scheduled on Day 8.
Continue skin care, electrolyte monitoring, infusion precautions and the urgent contact plan.
Low-risk antibody-only antiemesis is distinct from Day 1 moderate-risk chemotherapy prophylaxis.

NCCP 00692 v2 p1 permits omitting observation after two tolerated cetuximab doses, whereas current EMA Erbitux SmPC sections 4.2/4.4 require monitoring during and for at least one hour after every infusion. Reconcile this conflict with oncology pharmacy/local policy; do not automatically waive monitoring. Chemotherapy must start no earlier than one hour after cetuximab ends.

guidance.label: NCCP NCIS antiemetics V8 low-risk row
